title: A nontrivial centred valuation on a smooth curve and its etale coordinate
statement: Let $K$ be a field and $C$ a smooth integral finite-type $K$-scheme of dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Identify the function field $k(C)$, the local ring at the generic point, with $L$. Let $A\subsetneq L$ be a valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring] containing $K$ and suppose $\operatorname{Spec}A\to C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] induces this field identification at the generic point. The image $c$ of its closed point is a closed point of $C$, and $A=\mathcal O_{C,c}$ as subrings of $L$; this is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. There exist an affine neighbourhood $U$ of $c$ and an etale $K$-morphism $u:U\to\mathbf A^1_K$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. If $x\in A$ is its coordinate, $y=u(c)$ and $F=K(x)$, then $x$ is transcendental over $K$, $L/F$ is finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], $A\cap F=\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1_K,y}$, and $A$ is a localization at a prime ideal of an etale algebra over $A\cap F$. The induced residue-field extension $\kappa(c)/\kappa(y)$ is finite separable. If $K$ is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed], this residue-field extension is the identity under the given embeddings.
